---
title: "Data Model"
---

SupplyLens uses three stores, each owned by one organ. MongoDB is the raw store written by the mouth. Neo4j is the knowledge graph written by the gut and read by the presentation layer. PostgreSQL is a structured mirror of Neo4j supplier nodes, maintained for SQL dashboarding in Superset and Metabase.

---

## Neo4j — Knowledge Graph (CT114)

The central store. Written by the gut after every enrichment run; read by the presentation layer on demand. Every inferred node carries a confidence score, a list of contributing signals, and links to EvidenceClaim nodes that hold the source documents.

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
    Product {
        string sku PK
        string name
        string category
    }
    Supplier {
        string name PK
        string country
        int    tier
        string website
        float  confidence
        bool   inferred
        array  risk_flags
        string lei
    }
    RawMaterial {
        string name PK
        string origin
        string material_type
        float  confidence
        bool   inferred
    }
    Company {
        string name PK
        string country
        string industry
        string lei
        string parent_lei
    }
    Certificate {
        string name PK
        string issuer
        string standard
        date   valid_until
    }
    EvidenceClaim {
        string id PK
        string source_url
        string sha256
        string method
        string method_version
        float  confidence
        array  signals
        datetime collected_at
    }
    Event {
        string id PK
        string event_type
        string severity
        date   date
        string description
        string source_url
    }
    FinancialAlert {
        string id PK
        string alert_type
        string severity
        float  value
        string metric
        date   date
    }

    Product        ||--o{  Supplier       : "SUPPLIED_BY"
    Supplier       ||--o{  Supplier       : "SOURCED_FROM"
    Supplier       ||--o{  RawMaterial    : "SOURCED_FROM"
    Supplier       ||--o{  Certificate    : "CERTIFIED_BY"
    Supplier       }o--||  Company        : "OWNED_BY"
    Company        }o--o|  Company        : "SUBSIDIARY_OF"
    EvidenceClaim  }o--o{  Supplier       : "EVIDENCE_FOR"
    EvidenceClaim  }o--o{  RawMaterial    : "EVIDENCE_FOR"
    Supplier       ||--o{  Event          : "AFFECTED_BY"
    Supplier       ||--o{  FinancialAlert : "HAS_ALERT"
```

### Relationship Properties

| Relationship | Key properties |
|---|---|
| `SUPPLIED_BY` | `since` (year), `contract_value` (EUR) |
| `SOURCED_FROM` | `confidence` (0–1), `inferred` (bool), `source` (string), `volume_kg_year` |
| `EVIDENCE_FOR` | `signal_weight` (float), `reviewed_by` (researcher ID) |
| `AFFECTED_BY` | `impact_severity` (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL) |

### Risk Flags

Risk flags are written to `Supplier.risk_flags[]` by Step 7 of the gut pipeline.

| Flag | Condition |
|---|---|
| `SINGLE_SOURCE` | Only 1 inbound `SUPPLIED_BY` edge |
| `GEOPOLITICAL_RISK` | `country IN [CN, RU, IR, BY]` |
| `CBAM` | Supplier in carbon-border-tax scope |
| `LkSG` | German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act applies |
| `EUDR` | EU Deforestation Regulation commodity |

### Standard Traversal Query

```cypher
MATCH path = (p:Product {sku: $sku})-[:SUPPLIED_BY|SOURCED_FROM*1..3]->(n)
RETURN [node in nodes(path) | coalesce(node.name, node.sku)] AS chain,
       length(path) AS depth
ORDER BY depth
```

Limit depth to `*1..3` in production queries to avoid OOM on large graphs.

## MongoDB — Raw Store (CT121)

Written by the mouth; read by the gut. One document per collected item. The `status` field drives the gut's processing queue: the gut polls for documents where `status = "pending"` and marks them `"processed"` or `"failed"` on completion.

```json
{
  "_id":          "ObjectId",
  "source_url":   "https://...",
  "source_type":  "web_scrape | api_pull | manual_upload",
  "api_source":   "un_comtrade | importyeti | opensupplyhub | gdelt | gleif | null",
  "company_query":"Scania AB",
  "content":      "<html>...</html>  |  { trade flow JSON }  |  <binary ref>",
  "content_type": "text/html | application/json | application/pdf | application/vnd.ms-excel",
  "filename":     "scania_annual_report_2024.pdf  |  null",
  "sha256":       "a3f9...",
  "collected_at": "2026-08-20T06:00:00Z",
  "status":       "pending | processing | processed | failed",
  "processed_at": "2026-08-20T06:03:42Z  |  null",
  "error":        "null  |  'Tika timeout after 30s'"
}
```

**Indexes:** `source_url` (unique), `status`, `company_query`, `collected_at`

## PostgreSQL — Structured Entity Table (CT100)

A SQL mirror of Neo4j supplier nodes, maintained for Superset and Metabase dashboarding. Synced by `src/postgres_sync.py` after each gut run. Three tables cover supplier nodes, evidence claims, and supply chain events.

```sql
CREATE TABLE suppliers (
    id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    neo4j_name    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    country       CHAR(2),
    tier          SMALLINT,
    confidence    FLOAT,
    inferred      BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    risk_flags    TEXT[],
    lat           FLOAT,
    lon           FLOAT,
    website       TEXT,
    last_synced   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE evidence_claims (
    id             SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    supplier_name  TEXT REFERENCES suppliers(neo4j_name),
    source_url     TEXT NOT NULL,
    sha256         CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    method         TEXT,
    confidence     FLOAT,
    collected_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    reviewed_by    TEXT,
    status         TEXT DEFAULT 'unreviewed'  -- unreviewed | confirmed | rejected | flagged
);

CREATE TABLE events (
    id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    supplier_name TEXT,
    event_type    TEXT,
    severity      TEXT,
    event_date    DATE,
    description   TEXT,
    source_url    TEXT
);
```

---

## Confidence Score Model

Every inferred node carries a weighted confidence score fused from five independent OSINT signals. The score is a weighted sum bounded to [0, 1]; each contributing signal is stored in the `EvidenceClaim.signals[]` array so the score is fully auditable.

| Signal | Weight | Source |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Trade flow data | 0.30 | UN Comtrade, ImportYeti bill-of-lading |
| Facility location | 0.25 | OpenSupplyHub, satellite imagery |
| Corporate structure | 0.20 | OpenCorporates, GLEIF LEI |
| Document extraction | 0.15 | Annual reports, sustainability filings |
| News & incidents | 0.10 | GDELT, NGO databases, ILO |

A node inferred from a bill-of-lading hit (0.30) and a confirmed facility record (0.25) carries a score of 0.55 before any document or news signals are added. Scores below 0.40 are flagged as low-confidence and displayed with reduced opacity in the presentation layer. Scores above 0.80 require at least two independent signal types with no contradicting evidence.
